name: Khronon-Isolated Bimetric MOND (KIBM)
claimed_mechanism: This architecture resolves the P7 collision by embedding the screened preferred-frame khronon into a Hassan-Rosen bimetric chassis. The massive graviton sector provides an independent, finite kinetic normalization for the propagating modes, completely decoupled from the e^-y screened coupling of the khronon. The khronon supplies the off-ray lensing slip required by the DC-013 theorem, while its PPN-visible response is dynamically suppressed in the Solar System by the exponential kernel.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the massive graviton ensures c_T=1 and a healthy tensor sector. The khronon generates the necessary off-ray slip to achieve correct MOND lensing (eta=1) without inducing an f(R)-type slip. The e^-y screening ensures that the preferred-frame PPN parameters (alpha_1, alpha_2) vanish exponentially in the high-acceleration Solar System, satisfying Cassini constraints, while the independent kinetic normalization prevents the strong-coupling divergence (P7) that killed the single-metric khronometric candidate.
inequivalence_argument: This is inequivalent to DC-001 (local no-preferred-frame) because it explicitly includes a timelike khronon and a preferred-frame coupling. It is inequivalent to DC-010 (finite-alpha_inf khronometric) because the kinetic normalization is sourced by the bimetric massive graviton mass, not the screened khronon coupling, thus avoiding the P7 strong-coupling wall. It is inequivalent to DC-014 (stiff/non-propagating vector) because the khronon has standard kinetic terms and propagates, and the bimetric structure provides the independent scale for the kinetic term, avoiding the K->inf limit.
